threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still try to catch the Tube during rush hour, thinking it’ll save time. The packed platforms tell a different story.
Last night on the 68, a couple whispered their whole breakup saga. Must’ve been a quiet stop, because we all heard every word.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I saw a guy in a full suit calmly ordering a kebab at 2 AM while a street musician played beside him. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 3 AM, then stumble into a late-night techno party hidden behind a kebab shop. It's a rite of passage.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know that the best burrito spot isn’t the one on every Instagram account, it’s the hole in the wall on 24th that closes at 3 PM.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni stuck behind a guy walking a goat on Larkin. Only in San Francisco do you see someone casually taking their pet for a ride on the bus route.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists assume Gràcia is just a party zone. They miss the quiet mornings with locals sipping café amb llet and the kids biking to school.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their struggle with the metro ticket machines—staring at the screen like it's an alien spaceship.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'cabbage' refers to a green vegetable, not a cheeky nod to our local bike thieves.
Caught a night bus last week, and three blokes in matching tracksuits started chanting random football stats. Oddly, it felt like the second half of a match was happening right there.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of grilled meat from the Späti at midnight, mixed with the sound of late-night laughter—moment you realize this place has its own heartbeat.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how the U-Bahn announcements here have that quirky charm? Like the guy's reading poetry instead of just calling the next stop. Pure Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows that you don't just ride BART; you always check for delays first, especially with the Transbay Tube drama lately.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 22 today with a saxophonist doing a solo. Only in SF can you turn a mundane commute into a spontaneous street performance.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but the real charm is in the alleyways where you find the best cafés and street art.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They always insist on using the metro, even for a quick walk to the corner bakery. The locals know that a good croissant is just around the block.
